newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil under sell pressure.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps-Gas oil under sell pressure.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps were under sell pressure in lacklustre trading late afternoon on Monday, on the back of lower crude values, traders said.
"There are more sellers than buyers in the market today," one broker said.

Traders said the market came under some selling pressure due to lower crude prices and a weaker open on the International Petroleum Exchange (IPE) with December gas oil futures traded done $1.25 to $219.50 per tonne.
Gas oil swaps were sold down earlier on Monday with trades done for December at $30.00 and $29.95 a barrel, down about 20 cents from Friday's close, brokers said.
December gas oil was last quoted at $29.80/$29.95 per barrel. The December/January backwardation narrowed slightly as December was traded down with January seen relatively stable.
December/January was quoted at 40/50 cents from Friday's 50/60 cents, brokers said.

Jet fuel sentiment picked up slightly as news of earlier purchases by China and Japan filtered through the market. December jet fuel/gas oil spread was quoted at 60/80 cents, from Friday's 55/85 cents.
Fuel oil swaps lost about $1.00 per tonne from Friday's close on talks of ample regional supplies and thin demand, broker said.
November was quoted at $117.50/$119.25, down from Friday's $119.50/$120.00 with December seen at $117.00/$118.00.
Naphtha's December swap remained weaker at $22.90/$23.10 a barrel from $23.00/$23.30.
